subject: anaesthesia
title: Valve surgery, TEE and perioperative echo

steps.tx: Aortic stenosis turns severe near mean gradient 40 with **valve area** under 1, and low flow states need **dobutamine** recruitment to separate true from pseudo severe disease. Inoperable patients go toward TAVI while surgical candidates receive mechanical or tissue replacement, and mitral stenosis turns severe near pressure half time 220 with Wilkins scoring toward commissurotomy or balloon in selected cases. Quantify **regurgitation** with vena contracta, EROA and PISA, then match symptoms with LV dilation to repair thresholds while tachycardia and anaemia shape gradients.
steps.say: Stenosis grading decides the operation and is tested by the exam on thresholds. Aortic disease is severe near mean gradient 40 with valve area under 1. Low flow states need dobutamine recruitment to reveal true severity. Inoperable aortic patients go toward TAVI while others receive surgical replacement. Mitral disease is graded with pressure half time and Wilkins scoring while regurgitation is graded with vena contracta, EROA and PISA.

steps.tx: This image pairs a Doppler spectral trace with a high velocity jet plus colour flow mapping of a **regurgitant jet** for measurement. The trace quantifies aortic stenosis gradients while the colour map sizes mitral **regurgitation** by vena contracta and convergence. Read peak velocity with mean **gradients**, valve area, EROA and PISA together, because loads, rate and anaemia move numbers without changing disease.
steps.say: This image is the Doppler proof behind valve decisions. The spectral trace is a record of a high velocity jet for gradient measurement while colour flow is a map of the regurgitant jet. Together they give the quantification of aortic stenosis and mitral regurgitation for the exam. Peak velocity with mean gradients, valve area, EROA and PISA is always interpreted with loading, rate and anaemia in mind.

steps.tx: Perioperative **echocardiography** centres on mid oesophageal four chamber, transgastric short axis, bicaval, long axis and three dimensional valve views with **Doppler** gradients and bubble contrast for shunts. Aortic short with long axis, mitral commissural, tricuspid inflow and descending aortic views complete the sweep. Use valve, aortic, endocarditis, shock and congenital shunt **indications** to guide fluids, valves, shocks and shunts without losing the surgical window.
steps.say: Transoesophageal views are the framework of perioperative assessment. Mid oesophageal four chamber, transgastric short axis, bicaval and long axis views are the cover for valves and function. Doppler is the measurer of gradients while bubble contrast is the revealer of shunts. Valve disease with aortic pathology, endocarditis, shock and congenital shunts are the indications. The sweep is a guide to fluids, valve decisions and shock management.

vis.caption: Key TEE views for perioperative cardiac assessment

steps.tx: Systolic anterior motion complicates hypertrophic obstruction where hypovolaemia worsens dynamic **gradients**, so treatment uses fluids with phenylephrine and slowing with **beta blockade** while avoiding inotropes and vasodilators. Paravalvular leak shows rocking with haemolysis and LDH rise toward percutaneous or surgical **closure**, patient prosthesis mismatch shows high gradients across small roots toward root enlargement, and endocarditis with vegetations or abscess may need homograft redo.
steps.say: Systolic anterior motion is worse when the ventricle runs dry and fast. Hypovolaemia deepens the dynamic gradient while inotropes and vasodilators make it worse, which is dangerous. Treatment is filling the ventricle with phenylephrine and slowing the rate with beta blockade. Paravalvular leak with haemolysis is closed percutaneously or surgically while mismatch with high gradients is treated with root enlargement.

steps.tx: Aortic work spans Stanford type A **dissection** to theatre, aneurysm near 5.5 with roots near 5 in Marfan disease, circulatory arrest with antegrade perfusion, and spinal drains with endovascular cover. Pulmonary thromboendarterectomy uses deep hypothermic arrest while pulmonary **hypertension** uses nitric oxide with milrinone, bicaval **transplant** technique leaves denervated hearts resistant to atropine with biopsy watched rejection, and HeartMate devices bridge with driveline care, INR control and RV failure prediction.
steps.say: Aortic and advanced heart work completes the perioperative picture, which is broad. Stanford type A dissection goes to theatre while aneurysm thresholds guide root replacement. Circulatory arrest with antegrade perfusion is the protection for arch repair. Pulmonary hypertension is responsive to nitric oxide with milrinone. Transplanted hearts are denervated and are resistant to atropine while assist devices are bridgers with driveline care and RV watching.
